D/field-propagandist-dedication: Owner's standing ruling on skill/Perception DCs: "don't add a place for this, the user will need to remember." Both bonuses here are DCs others roll against (Perception DC vs Lie, and Deception DC if you have Lie to Me), and the second is additionally gated on owning another feat. Separately: the Society trained/expert grant is a proficiency grant handled by the FEAT_GRANTS lane, not this one; do not encode it here.

D/sixfingers-elixir: UMBRELLA RECORD. Ruling A: 'the summery of all of the items shouldn't be an option for the characters, it's not a real item so they shouldn't even see that' — umbrella/summary records get NO situational entries and are hidden from pickers. Verified against core.json: sixfingers-elixir has no price, its three graded twins (lesser/moderate/greater, levels 5/11/17) have 25/250/2,500 gp, which is precisely the ruling's stated test. Ruling D's 'Six-Fingers Elixir add a * in the reflex description pop up that says the effect and that it only effects the dc' is satisfied by the three grade records, which are the ones a character can actually own and which already carry the entry.

D/weapon-innovation: Verdict stands — the bonus is not granted by Weapon Innovation, it is granted by one of eleven initial weapon modifications (Segmented Frame) and only while the innovation is collapsed to light Bulk, so registering it here would put a permanent Stealth star on every inventor who never took it. But the bonus is NOT homeless and nothing is waiting on modification tracking: core.json's classFeatures bucket has its own 'segmented-frame' record, and src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts already registers it — targets skill/stealth, when 'to Stealth checks (and your DC) to hide or conceal your innovation, while it's collapsed to light Bulk', bonus '+2 circumstance'. Adding it to weapon-innovation would double-list it for the inventors who did choose Segmented Frame. No new surface, no follow-up work.

D/execution-powder: Nothing here lands on the character as a persistent, knowable number. Two things are granted: (a) a death effect imposed on a POISONED CREATURE at 0 HP — the poison's own save (the printed **Saving Throw** field is empty in this record; the importer dropped the save type and DC), which is the item's DC, not a DC the character owns or modifies; and (b) 20 temporary Hit Points plus +1 status to attack and damage — but the beneficiary is 'a random creature adjacent to the victim', decided at the table, and could be an ally, an enemy, or nobody the sheet knows about. Starring the character's strikeAttack/strikeDamage would promise a bonus the character has no claim to. If the owner wants it reachable at all, the natural home is the consumable-MODE lane already built (lane E): a player-toggled pill the character switches on only if the GM says the spores landed on them. Do not register it as a passive or a star.

D/bombers-eye-elixir-lesser: The elixir changes a number on the TARGET, not on the character: it shaves 1 off the circumstance bonus to AC the target gets from cover. The app models no target AC and no cover, so there is nothing to attach to. Answering the record's openQuestion: do NOT star strikeAttack as an effective '+1 to hit' — the text grants no bonus to the attack roll, and a target in the open (no cover) gains nothing at all from the elixir, so the star would be false roughly half the time. There is also no ACTION to mark: the thing modified is the target's Take Cover benefit, not one of the character's actions, so Ruling D's action-marker does not reach it. Shipped precedent for this exact shape is `motion-seeking-lenses` (line 1912), where the identical cover-loss clause was folded into the `when` text of a bonus that already existed rather than given its own star — Bomber's Eye has no other bonus to ride along on. If the owner wants it visible, the honest home is a display-only MODE pill ('Bomber's Eye: bomb Strikes ignore 1 of a target's cover bonus, 5 minutes') that changes no number.

D/bombers-eye-elixir-greater: Same shape as the lesser elixir at 2 instead of 1 — a reduction to the TARGET's cover bonus to AC, on bomb Strikes only. Same reasoning: no target-AC/cover model, no character stat row moves, no action of the character's is modified, and starring strikeAttack with '+2' would invent a bonus the text does not print (against a target with no cover it is worth nothing). Best available surface if the owner ever wants one is the display-only mode pill, not a star.

D/potion-of-disguise: Per the owner's standing ruling on skill DCs (Potion of Disguise named explicitly): "don't add a place for this, the user will need to remember." The +4 raises the character's Deception DC — the number an onlooker's Perception check is rolled against while Impersonating — and never the Deception check the player rolls. Starring the Deception row would be read as a check bonus, which it is not. The 'add your level even if untrained' clause is part of the same DC and has the same fate. No action-marker either: Impersonate exists as an action id, but the potion does not change what Impersonate DOES, it only sets the DC opponents face, which is the exact thing the owner declined to surface.

D/potion-of-disguise-lesser: Same sentence, same ruling as the parent record — a Deception DC (not a check), which the owner ruled explicitly gets no place on the sheet. The lesser variant adds only a size floor of Small and craft requirements, neither of which is a bonus to anything.

D/potion-of-disguise-moderate: Same Deception-DC-only bonus as the parent, ruled no-surface by the owner. The moderate variant's only extra mechanics are a wider size range (Tiny to Large) and 'reducing your reach to 0 as a Tiny creature' — a reach change, not a bonus, and reach is not one of the available target kinds either.

D/potion-of-disguise-greater: Same Deception-DC-only bonus, ruled no-surface. The greater variant's addition ('You can attempt to Impersonate a specific individual, though you still need to roll Deception') expands what you may attempt and explicitly grants NO bonus to the roll, so it does not become an action-marker on `impersonate` either — there is no changed value to show in parentheses.

D/olfactory-obfuscator-lesser: Owner ruled this item by name under the skill-DC decision: no surface. The +4 raises the DC a Seeking creature's Perception check must beat (the character's Stealth DC), never a check the player rolls, and it evaporates the moment the seeker uses any non-scent sense — so a Stealth star would over-promise twice over. IMPORTANT INCONSISTENCY TO FIX: `olfactory-obfuscator-greater` is currently SHIPPED as a Stealth star in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 856 ('+4 item', 'against Seek attempts by creatures using only scent'). That entry predates the ruling and contradicts it; it should be removed so the lesser and greater variants behave the same.
